terms.gloss: anywhere you like, anywhere at all
evidence: Cic. Fam. 6.1.1: nēmō sit quīn ubivīs quam ibi ubi est esse mālit (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 14.22.2: ubivīs tūtius quam in senātū (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: “Where you will”, of place where; ubivīs gentium, anywhere in the world (Ter. Hec. 3.1.4). Lewis & Short also gives “everywhere”. For “anywhere” after a negative or in a question, see somewhere.

evidence: Ter. Haut. 5.1.55: immō abeat quōvīs gentium (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of going: “anywhere you like”. Lewis & Short marks it poetic; its passages are from comedy.
As a conjunction, “wherever”; standing alone, “anywhere at all, wherever it may be”.

evidence: Sen. Tranq. 1.6: ubilibet nōn dēfutūrus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Post-Augustan (Seneca); ubivīs is the usual word.

phrases.latin: nēmō sit quīn ubivīs quam ibi ubi est esse mālit
phrases.english: there is nobody who would not rather be anywhere than where he is
no, let him go anywhere in the world

phrases.latin: nūllum nostrum usquam neglegentem esse sermōnem; quidquid loquēmur ubicumque, sit prō suā scīlicet portiōne perfectum
phrases.english: none of our talk should ever be careless; whatever we say, anywhere, should be perfect in its own measure

phrases.latin: cibus parābilis facilisque, ubilibet nōn dēfutūrus
phrases.english: food that is cheap and easy, that will not be lacking anywhere

sources: Lewis & Short: ubivis · Lewis & Short: quovis · Lewis & Short: ubicumque · Lewis & Short: ubilibet
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-quintilianus), checked against the editions named there.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
